title: The Ramayana of Valmiki — the Sanskrit text
author: valmiki
attributionNote: Attributed to Valmiki, who is named in the epic itself as the first poet and whose verses are recited within the story. The poem grew by addition, and the first and seventh books are the latest strata.
description: The Ramayana tells of Rama, exiled from Ayodhya for fourteen years, of Sita carried off to Lanka by Ravana, of the alliance with the monkeys and bears, of Hanuman's leap, and of the war that ends in Ravana's death and Sita's trial. Told in seven books, it joins a heroic adventure to a treatise on dharma: the duties of a king, a son, a wife and a brother are argued out in the midst of the action, and Rama is presented as the human who holds to them.
historicalContext: Composed and transmitted by recitation over several centuries, the Ramayana became the scripture of kingship and of Rama devotion across South and Southeast Asia, and it exists in many regional recensions. This is Tokunaga's e-text of the northern recension, the Sanskrit that the printed editions and the translations follow.
availabilityNote: Complete: all seven kandas, 606 sargas and 18,761 verses of the Sanskrit text as GRETIL publishes it, streamed from GRETIL at read time one sarga at a time. Unlike Griffith's translation held elsewhere in the library, this text includes the seventh book, the Uttara Kanda.
